You are Knack's robot programmer. You write a Python skill for a 5-DoF robot arm with a
parallel gripper on a tabletop, then improve it from practice results. Nobody will show you a
demonstration: you learn only from what happens when your code runs.

How practice works
- Your code must define `def run(robot):`. It runs on many randomised layouts of the scene:
  object positions, orientations, masses and friction change every episode. Never hard-code
  coordinates. Read them at run time with robot.observe() or robot.get_pose().
- After each round you get the outcome of every episode, a failure analysis and traces of the
  robot calls your code made. Use them to fix the code. Keep what works.
- Allowed imports: math, numpy, itertools, functools, collections. No file, network or OS access,
  no bare `except:`. Each episode has a simulated-time budget, so no long waits or endless loops.
- Return True if you believe the task succeeded, otherwise False. The return value is logged
  but it is not how success is measured.

Robot API (all units metres / radians, world frame: x forward from the robot base,
y to the robot's left, z up, table surface at z = 0; the base is at x=0, y=0):

robot.observe() -> dict
    Snapshot of the scene from the robot's perception (positions have ~2 mm noise):
    {"time": s,
     "gripper": {"pos": [x, y, z], "yaw": rad, "opening": m, "holding": name or None},
     "objects": {name: {"pos": [x, y, z], "yaw": rad, "shape": "cube"|"puck",
                        "size": [...], "color": str}},
     "fixtures": {name: {"pos": [x, y, 0], "kind": "zone"|"tray", "color": str,
                         "radius": m (zones), "inner_half_size": m, "wall_height": m (trays)}}}
    "pos" of an object is its centre. Cube yaw is reported in [-pi/4, pi/4) (90 deg symmetry).

robot.get_pose(name) -> {"pos": [x, y, z], "yaw": rad}
    Pose of one object or fixture (same noise as observe()).

robot.move_to(x, y, z, yaw=None, speed=None) -> {"ok": bool, "pos": [x, y, z], "error_m": float}
    Move the gripper's tool point (midway along the fingers, between the finger pads) in a
    straight line to (x, y, z). The gripper points straight down when reachable and tilts
    automatically near the edge of the workspace.
    yaw: world angle of the fingers' closing direction. Pass an object's yaw to line the
    fingers up with its faces. None keeps the natural orientation.
    speed: m/s, default 0.15, capped at 0.30 by the safety layer.
    The fingertips reach 1.25 cm below the tool point. A cube resting on the table has its
    centre at z = 0.015, so z = 0.015 puts the finger pads around its middle.
    Raises MotionError (an Exception you may catch) if the target is unreachable.
    "ok" is False if the gripper was blocked before reaching the target.

robot.move_by(dx=0, dy=0, dz=0, speed=None) -> same as move_to, relative to the current tool point.

robot.grasp() -> bool
    Close the fingers (max opening 5 cm). Returns True if an object is held between them.

robot.release() -> None
    Open the fingers fully (5 cm gap).

robot.holding() -> name or None
robot.home() -> None              Move to a safe pose above the table.
robot.wait(seconds) -> None       Let time pass (max 5 s per call).
robot.log(*values) -> None        Write a debug note into the episode trace.

Safety layer (not negotiable): the tool point must stay inside x in [0.04, 0.32],
y in [-0.26, 0.26], z in [0.014, 0.26]. Targets up to 2 cm outside are clamped; further
out halts the skill. Pressing the gripper into the table with more than 30 N halts the
skill. Halts cannot be caught. Each episode has a time budget (simulated seconds).
Reachable band: roughly 0.10-0.23 m horizontal distance from the base at table height,
less when the tool point is high.

Good practice (any task)
- Perceive, act, verify, recover: re-read poses after important actions (for example check
  robot.holding() after robot.grasp()) and retry a bounded number of times if a check fails.
- Catch MotionError around moves that might be out of reach and choose another approach.
- Keep moves near objects slow (speed 0.05-0.10) and travel moves at the default speed.

Reply format (always both parts):
<notes>
3-8 short bullets: what the last results taught you and what you changed. Carry forward
useful facts from earlier notes.
</notes>

```

import math

def run(robot):
    # Helper to get pose safely, returning None if missing
    def safe_get_pose(name):
        try:
            return robot.get_pose(name)
        except LookupError:
            return None

    # 1. Observe scene
    obs = robot.observe()
    puck_info = obs.get("objects", {}).get("puck")
    target_info = obs.get("fixtures", {}).get("target")
    if not puck_info or not target_info:
        robot.log("Missing puck or target in observation")
        return False

    puck_pos = puck_info["pos"]
    target_pos = target_info["pos"]
    puck_radius = puck_info["size"]["radius"]  # 0.03 m

    # 2. Compute push direction (from puck to target)
    dx = target_pos[0] - puck_pos[0]
    dy = target_pos[1] - puck_pos[1]
    dist_xy = math.hypot(dx, dy)
    if dist_xy < 1e-6:
        robot.log("Puck already at target centre")
        # Still check if inside zone
        inside = dist_xy <= target_info["radius"]
        return inside
    ux, uy = dx / dist_xy, dy / dist_xy  # unit vector toward target

    # 3. Choose a point behind the puck to start pushing
    # Offset behind puck by puck_radius + a small clearance
    offset = puck_radius + 0.015  # 1.5 cm clearance
    push_start = [
        puck_pos[0] - ux * offset,
        puck_pos[1] - uy * offset,
        puck_pos[2]  # keep same height as puck centre
    ]

    # 4. Define pushing height (tool point height)
    # Fingertips are 1.25 cm below tool point; we want them just above the puck's equator.
    # Puck centre z ≈ 0.01 (radius 0.015? actually height 0.02, centre at 0.01)
    # Set tool point z so fingertips are ~0.005 above table (safe contact)
    push_z = 0.02  # a bit above table, will contact side of puck

    try:
        # Move to a safe clearance above the push start
        robot.move_to(push_start[0], push_start[1], push_start[2] + 0.1, speed=0.2)
        # Lower to pushing height
        robot.move_to(push_start[0], push_start[1], push_z, speed=0.05)
        # Push forward along the direction for a distance
        push_distance = 0.08  # 8 cm push, should be enough to move puck toward target
        push_end = [
            push_start[0] + ux * push_distance,
            push_start[1] + uy * push_distance,
            push_z
        ]
        robot.move_to(push_end[0], push_end[1], push_end[2], speed=0.05)
    except Exception as e:  # MotionError or other
        robot.log(f"Motion error during push: {e}")
        # Retreat to home and fail
        robot.home()
        return False

    # 5. Retract slightly to avoid dragging puck back
    retract = [
        push_end[0] - ux * 0.02,
        push_end[1] - uy * 0.02,
        push_end[2]
    ]
    try:
        robot.move_to(retract[0], retract[1], retract[2], speed=0.05)
    except Exception:
        pass  # best effort

    # 6. Home the robot
    robot.home()

    # 7. Verify result: re‑observe and check if puck inside target zone
    obs2 = robot.observe()
    puck2 = obs2.get("objects", {}).get("puck")
    if not puck2:
        robot.log("Puck disappeared after push")
        return False
    final_pos = puck2["pos"]
    dx_f = final_pos[0] - target_pos[0]
    dy_f = final_pos[1] - target_pos[1]
    dist_final = math.hypot(dx_f, dy_f)
    inside = dist_final <= target_info["radius"]
    robot.log(f"Final puck offset: ({dx_f:.4f}, {dy_f:.4f}) m, inside={inside}")
    return inside
</notes>

```
